config.selection: names-CER only, seeded with init score

results.best: base (no trained step beat init; selector kept step 0 as designed)

interpretation: Freeze-encoder + its paired 5e-6 LR degrades held-out names from the first eval point, monotonically. The init-seeded selector prevented a bad checkpoint from being crowned (best = base). Answer to the variant question: freezing the encoder does NOT preserve names; lowlr (all-param, LR 1e-6) remains the right mode. Confound noted: this variant changes both freeze and LR, so the harm can't be attributed to freezing alone - but as a package it is clearly worse.
claim_boundary: achieved-on-cleaner-data scores, no causation; names = 7-person dev eval; EVAL500 separate.
